summary: Death Stranding entries from the prepared 1000-title candidate queue, researched for Sami's fidelity-first archive route.

entries.title: Death Stranding
entries.definitive_edition: Death Stranding Director's Cut on Windows PC

emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Windows PC Director's Cut at current patch level

primary.why: Director's Cut is the current expanded PC route, with high frame rate, photo mode, ultra-wide support, cross-over content, and upgrade/save-transfer guidance from the original PC version.
primary.how_to_play: Use Death Stranding Director's Cut on PC. Record storefront/build, save transfer state, graphics/upscaling settings, online Social Strand state, Half-Life/Cyberpunk cross-over content, and whether the run is original or Director's Cut.

entries.remaster_caveats: Document whether saves were transferred and whether original PC/PS4 release-state differences matter to the archive.

entries.title: Death Stranding 2: On the Beach
entries.definitive_edition: Death Stranding 2: On the Beach on Windows PC at 4K with ultrawide support and an unlocked frame rate

emulation.notes: Native Windows route; no emulation branch.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Windows PC at 4K with ultrawide and unlocked frame rate

primary.version: Death Stranding 2: On the Beach PC (Steam / Epic Games Store)
primary.why: The PC version, ported by the studio behind several other high-quality PlayStation PC conversions, adds 21:9 ultrawide and 32:9 super-ultrawide support for gameplay AND in-game cutscenes at 4K, plus unlocked frame rates beyond the console targets — the same relationship the first game's PC route has to its PS5 release, and no content is lost.
primary.how_to_play: Play Death Stranding 2: On the Beach on Windows PC. Record storefront/build, resolution/aspect (note if 21:9 or 32:9 is in use), upscaler and frame-rate cap, and chapter/order progress.

entries.remaster_caveats: Record whether a run is on the PS5 original or the later PC version — post-launch patches mean the two are not frame-identical.
